name: epicscorelibs
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set name = "epicscorelibs" %}
{% set version = "7.0.10.99.0.1" %}

package:
  name: {{ name|lower }}
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/{{ name[0] }}/{{ name }}/{{ name }}-{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: e8c8d9730faef7df55f4d329c359a0e4c044f03a524dd2e4587e90132873edfd
  patches:
    # These three patches together adapt epicscorelibs to use the
    # epics-base conda package's shared libraries, headers, and DBD files
    # instead of building and bundling a private copy (so both can
    # coexist in one process). They are independent and do NOT stack: each
    # touches a disjoint set of files (named after those files below), is
    # generated directly against the pristine source tarball above, and
    # does not depend on the others having been applied first. Their
    # relative order in this list is arbitrary.
    #
    # Repoints epicscorelibs/{ioc,path/__init__}.py at epics-base's install
    # location instead of a private copy built by this package.
    - patch/ioc_and_path_use_epics_base.patch
    # setup.py/pyproject.toml: no longer build or install any of that
    # private copy (DSOs/headers/dbd files), nor the setuptools_dso build
    # framework used to do so - meaning this package builds no native code
    # at all, and needs neither setuptools_dso nor a compiler to build.
    - patch/setup_and_pyproject_no_setuptools_dso.patch
    # epicscorelibs/config.py still exposes a small amount of toolchain
    # information (OS_CLASS, CMPLR_CLASS, CPPFLAGS, ...) as public API,
    # upstream determined by invoking a compiler's preprocessor (via
    # setuptools_dso) at import time. Since this is a noarch: python
    # package installed as-is on every platform, nothing can be baked in
    # at build time either (unlike the setup.py patch, above, for the
    # same reason). Instead this is derived from platform.system() at
    # import time: a given platform's compiler family and C++ ABI are
    # fixed and coherent across the whole conda-forge ecosystem, so this
    # is equivalent to actually probing a compiler, without requiring
    # setuptools_dso or a compiler to be present at all.
    - patch/config_no_compiler_probe.patch

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python
  script: '{{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . --no-deps --no-build-isolation -vv'

requirements:
  host:
    - python {{ python_min }}
    - pip
    - setuptools
    - epics-base
  run:
    - python >={{ python_min }}
    - numpy
    - epics-base

test:
  imports:
    - epicscorelibs
    - epicscorelibs.ca.cadef  # loads libca from epics-base at import
    - epicscorelibs.ca.dbr
    - epicscorelibs.config
  commands:
    # EPICS libraries come from epics-base; none are bundled here
    - python -c "import os, epicscorelibs; d = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(epicscorelibs.__file__), 'lib'); assert not any(f.endswith(('.so', '.dylib', '.dll')) for f in os.listdir(d))"

about:
  home: https://github.com/epics-base/epicscorelibs
  license: EPICS
  license_file: LICENSE
  summary: EPICS core libraries packaged as a "python" module
  description: |
    The EPICS (Experimental Physics and Industrial Control System) core
    libraries for use by python modules. Either dynamically with ctypes
    or statically by compiled extension.

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - tacaswell
    - hhslepicka
    - klauer
    - mrakitin
